This format sets out the workshop materials for a reader who works alone, without a facilitator and without a class, in five stages and at your own pace. The case study is a field experiment, in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, and its claim is one of the original authors (OAs) [@EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect] that five analysts reanalysed for the SCORE robustness study [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]. The modules of the [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) sit between the tasks of the exercise, and the route ends on a project of your own. You leave with a case-study report and that project, both in a version-controlled repository that another person can clone and re-render.

## How you work

:::: {.fmt-steps}

::: {.fmt-step}
### webR {.unnumbered .unlisted}

No programming is assumed. The webR workspace holds every task in cells that run R in the browser through [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/), a version of R compiled to run inside a web page, with hints and worked solutions, so that you can try each step before your installation is ready, or carry on there if it fails.

[Open the webR workspace](../../lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

::: {.fmt-step}
### R and an IDE {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Stage 1 installs R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), and stage 2 teaches enough R to start the case study.

[Setup](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

::: {.fmt-step}
### The IDE workspace {#the-workspace .unnumbered .unlisted}

You work in the IDE workspace of the case study on your own machine, from the setup check of stage 1 to the project of stage 5.

[The IDE workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing-workspace/){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

::::

Stage 1 takes Task 1 of the exercise, stage 3 Tasks 2 and 3, and stage 4 Tasks 4 to 6, and the [exercise](exercise.qmd) page sets out the six tasks.

The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met.

Where a stage can be shortened for a reader who already knows part of its material, its page says how, in a paragraph headed **Shortcuts**.

Sending your results to the class chart on the [Class results](../../class-results.qmd) page is optional.

## The stages

Each stage is roughly a day's work, and the whole route about a working week, or longer when it is spread over evenings or weekends.

- [Stage 3 – The claim and its reproduction](stage-3.qmd)
- [Stage 4 – The menu and the declaration](stage-4.qmd)
- [Stage 5 – Your own project](stage-5.qmd)
